memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Joseph's brothers arrived at his house, and Judah and his brothers threw themselves to the ground before him." — Gen 44:14 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Judah is named first now. That is significant. It was Judah who suggested selling Joseph in the first place (Gen 37:26-27). Now he leads his brothers back to face the consequences.

And here they are again, face down on the ground before Joseph — exactly as the boy's dreams had shown, all those years ago (Gen 37:7). Joseph is watching the fulfilment of the very dreams that got him thrown into a pit. God had spoken, and though everything in between seemed to contradict it, God's word did not fail.

That is the quiet encouragement running under this whole story. God's purposes are not fragile. They survive jealousy, betrayal, slavery, false accusation and prison. Man's worst intentions could not derail what God had said.

Nothing has changed about God. What He has promised in Christ — that He will finish the work He began in us, that He will present His people faultless, that Christ will reign — will stand, however long the road looks and however much the present moment seems to contradict it (Phil 1:6).

And here, before the throne of the man who holds their lives in his hands, is Judah — the one from whose line the true King will come (Gen 49:10; Rev 5:5).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What promise of God are you waiting on, where the present seems to contradict it?
2. How does Joseph's story strengthen your confidence in God's faithfulness?
3. Is there a past failure God is inviting you to face rather than avoid?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, Your word does not fail. When my circumstances seem to contradict Your promises, hold my heart steady and keep me trusting. Amen.
